title: A story with a twist
job: A six-sentence narrative with a line of dialogue inside it
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: SIX SENTENCES, WITH ONE LINE OF QUOTED SPEECH INSIDE. That is L3-M10's account tightened and given a turn. The sequencers hold it together — prathamam, tataḥ, anantaram, ante (L2-M10) — and each of them sits BETWEEN sentences and never inside one.

A STORY HAS A SHAPE AND NOT JUST A SEQUENCE, and akasmāt is what marks the turn. Something is going one way, akasmāt it does not, and the last sentence says what that meant. Without it you have a list of things that happened in order.

THE QUOTED LINE IS L3-M5's iti AND NOTHING ELSE: the words exactly as spoken, then iti, then the verb of saying. NO TENSE SHIFT AND NO PERSON SHIFT — the quote keeps its own speaker's aham and its own present, so bhavān adya gṛham gacchatu iti saḥ uktavān is 'go home today, he said'.

A QUOTED LINE IS SPOKEN IN THE SAME REGISTER AS THE STORY AROUND IT. A character addressing somebody says bhavān or bhavatī with a third-person verb, exactly as the narration does. The intimate tvam stays where L2-M1 left it — at one sentence in this whole course — because opening it inside a quote would drag the whole second-person paradigm in behind it.

THE PARTICIPIAL PAST FORKS ONCE, AT THE SPEAKER. All six sentences are a man's or all six are a woman's, and the variations entry supplies the WHOLE story in the other and not one sentence of it. The plural participial past is written nowhere in this course, so a story still cannot be told by two people at once.

PRO-DROP HOLDS OVER SIX SENTENCES. aham appears in the first sentence at most: the -mi ending and the participle's own gender have already said who is speaking, and repeating the pronoun in every sentence reads as insistence rather than as clarity.

A CORRELATIVE PAIR LIVES INSIDE ONE SENTENCE AND NEVER CROSSES A FULL STOP, and that now covers five pairs: yataḥ … ataḥ, yaḥ … saḥ, yadi … tarhi, yadā … tadā and yāvat … tāvat. The sequencers do the opposite job — they only ever sit between sentences — so the two systems never compete for a slot.

āścaryam IS 'A SURPRISE', neuter, and it goes into L3-M6's frame for a feeling: mahyam āścaryam āsīt, 'to me there was surprise'. That is how a story says what the turn meant without a verb for being surprised.

ENGLISH REPORTS SPEECH BY MOVING THE TENSE BACK — 'he said he WAS going' — AND SANSKRIT MOVES NOTHING. Whatever was said is quoted as it was said and iti closes it. A learner who shifts the tense has translated the English machinery and not the sentence.

WHAT A STORY STILL DOES NOT GET. No new proper noun: rāmaḥ and sītā are the only two names this course writes, and a character here is mama pitā, ekaḥ janaḥ or an adhyāpakaḥ. No vocative, which a line of dialogue wants more than anything else in the level. No imperfect but L4-M8's āsīt, so agacchat, akarot and abhavat stay unwritten. No plural participial past. And no formal register, which is L4-M7's alone.

sentences.display: prathamam aham mitreṇa saha vidyālayam gatavān. tataḥ saṃskṛtam paṭhitavān. akasmāt mama pustakam na āsīt. bhavān adya gṛham gacchatu iti adhyāpakaḥ uktavān. anantaram gṛham gatavān. ante pustakam gṛhe āsīt, tat mahyam āścaryam āsīt.
sentences.script: प्रथमम् अहम् मित्रेण सह विद्यालयम् गतवान्। ततः संस्कृतम् पठितवान्। अकस्मात् मम पुस्तकम् न आसीत्। भवान् अद्य गृहम् गच्छतु इति अध्यापकः उक्तवान्। अनन्तरम् गृहम् गतवान्। अन्ते पुस्तकम् गृहे आसीत्, तत् मह्यम् आश्चर्यम् आसीत्।
sentences.cue: First I went to school with a friend. Then I studied Sanskrit. Suddenly my book was not there. 'Go home today,' the teacher said. After that I went home. In the end the book was at home — that was a surprise to me.
sentences.literal: first I with-friend together school went. then Sanskrit studied. suddenly my book not was. your-honour today home let-go quote teacher said. after-that home went. in-the-end book at-home was, that to-me surprise was

words.note: L2-M10's first sequencer. It sits between sentences and never inside one.
'Suddenly'. It takes no ending and heads the sentence that turns the story. It marks a break in what was going on, not merely speed.
L1-M1's book. Here it is what the story turns on, and it is missing before it is found.
L4-M8's one imperfect, third singular. A story needs it for everything that merely stood there while the actions happened.
L2-M4's polite imperative, inside the quote. A character addresses bhavān with a third-person verb, exactly as the narration does.
L3-M5's quotative, standing behind the quoted words. Nothing inside the quote shifts for being quoted.
L3-M5's past of saying. It agrees with whoever spoke, not with the person telling the story.
L1-M1's teacher, the one who spoke. uktavān agrees with him and not with the narrator.
'A surprise', neuter. It sits in L3-M6's frame for a feeling — mahyam āścaryam āsīt — so nobody has to be the one surprised.

sentences.trap: The quoted line keeps its own present and its own listener. bhavān inside it is the narrator being spoken to, not the teacher — and nothing about it changes for having been quoted.

sentences.cue: First I went to the city. Then I ate a meal with a friend. Suddenly it was raining. 'Do not go home today,' my father said. So I studied in the city in the evening. In the end it was not raining, so I went home.

sentences.cue: First I went to school in the morning. Then I studied Sanskrit. Suddenly I had a headache. 'Go home and drink the medicine,' the teacher said. After that I went home and drank the medicine. In the end the ache was gone, so I was happy.

L3-M7's head in its 'in' shape. The pain is the subject and the body part is where it is.
L3-M7's pain, the subject of its own sentence — no verb of hurting exists in this course.
L4-M8's one imperfect, third singular. A story needs it for everything that merely stood there while the actions happened.
L1-M10's 'and', standing BEHIND the second of the two things it joins, exactly as L1-M10 taught.

L1-M9's adjective, neuter to agree with āścaryam.

sentences.trap: api leans on the word in front of it, so aham api is 'I too' and not 'also I work'. Move it and the sentence says something the sister did not.

variations.display: prathamam aham nagare kāryam kṛtavatī. tataḥ kāryālaye patram likhitavatī. akasmāt mama bhaginī tatra āsīt. aham api atra kāryam karomi iti sā uktavatī. anantaram aham bhojanam khāditavatī. ante mahyam sukham āsīt, yataḥ tat āścaryam sundaram āsīt.
variations.script: प्रथमम् अहम् नगरे कार्यम् कृतवती। ततः कार्यालये पत्रम् लिखितवती। अकस्मात् मम भगिनी तत्र आसीत्। अहम् अपि अत्र कार्यम् करोमि इति सा उक्तवती। अनन्तरम् अहम् भोजनम् खादितवती। अन्ते मह्यम् सुखम् आसीत्, यतः तत् आश्चर्यम् सुन्दरम् आसीत्।
variations.cue: First I did some work in the city. Then I wrote a form at the office. Suddenly my sister was there. 'I work here too,' she said. After that I had a meal. In the end I was happy, because it was a lovely surprise.
variations.changed: a woman tells it, and the story now has two feminine speakers whose participles agree with different people

variations.display: prathamam aham kāryālaye patram likhitavān. akasmāt mama bhaginī tatra āsīt. ante mahyam sukham āsīt.
variations.script: प्रथमम् अहम् कार्यालये पत्रम् लिखितवान्। अकस्मात् मम भगिनी तत्र आसीत्। अन्ते मह्यम् सुखम् आसीत्।
variations.cue: First I wrote a form at the office. Suddenly my sister was there. In the end I was happy.
variations.changed: the shape alone: the ordinary morning, the turn, and what it left behind

variations.display: yadā mama bhaginī tatra āsīt tadā mahyam āścaryam āsīt.
variations.script: यदा मम भगिनी तत्र आसीत् तदा मह्यम् आश्चर्यम् आसीत्।
variations.cue: When my sister was there I was surprised.
variations.changed: the turn and its meaning folded into one sentence with L4-M6's time pair, which is a correlative and therefore stays inside one full stop

sentences.usage: The happiest shape the twist takes: the surprise is a person.

comprehensionPool.display: prathamam aham prātaḥ gṛhe bhojanam kṛtavān. tataḥ vidyālayam gatavān. akasmāt vṛṣṭiḥ āsīt. ataḥ aham tatra sāyam paṭhitavān. ante gṛham gatavān.
comprehensionPool.script: प्रथमम् अहम् प्रातः गृहे भोजनम् कृतवान्। ततः विद्यालयम् गतवान्। अकस्मात् वृष्टिः आसीत्। अतः अहम् तत्र सायम् पठितवान्। अन्ते गृहम् गतवान्।
comprehensionPool.cue: First I made a meal at home in the morning. Then I went to school. Suddenly it was raining. So I studied there in the evening. In the end I went home.

comprehensionPool.display: bhavān adya kim kṛtavān iti mama pitā pṛcchati. kāryālaye patram likhitavān iti aham uktavān.
comprehensionPool.script: भवान् अद्य किम् कृतवान् इति मम पिता पृच्छति। कार्यालये पत्रम् लिखितवान् इति अहम् उक्तवान्।
comprehensionPool.cue: 'What did you do today?' my father asks. 'I wrote a form at the office,' I said.

comprehensionPool.display: prathamam jalam pibatu. tataḥ auṣadham khādatu. anantaram upaviśatu. ante punaḥ jalam pibatu.
comprehensionPool.script: प्रथमम् जलम् पिबतु। ततः औषधम् खादतु। अनन्तरम् उपविशतु। अन्ते पुनः जलम् पिबतु।
comprehensionPool.cue: First drink water. Then take the medicine. After that sit down. In the end drink water again.

comprehensionPool.display: avaśyam idam kāryam dīrgham, kintu idam hitam. mama mate ataḥ idam kartavyam.
comprehensionPool.script: अवश्यम् इदम् कार्यम् दीर्घम्, किन्तु इदम् हितम्। मम मते अतः इदम् कर्तव्यम्।
comprehensionPool.cue: Certainly this work is long, but it is good for us. In my opinion it must therefore be done.

comprehensionPool.display: aham mitreṇa saha yānena mahānagaram gatavān. mama yātrā dīrghā āsīt. tatra ekam sundaram sthānam āsīt. ante aham gṛham gatavān.
comprehensionPool.script: अहम् मित्रेण सह यानेन महानगरम् गतवान्। मम यात्रा दीर्घा आसीत्। तत्र एकम् सुन्दरम् स्थानम् आसीत्। अन्ते अहम् गृहम् गतवान्।
comprehensionPool.cue: I went to the big city by vehicle with a friend. My journey was long. There was one beautiful place there. In the end I went home.

comprehensionPool.display: bālye aham pratidinam mandiram gatavān. adhunā aham nagare kāryam karomi. adhunā api mahyam tat mandiram rocate.
comprehensionPool.script: बाल्ये अहम् प्रतिदिनम् मन्दिरम् गतवान्। अधुना अहम् नगरे कार्यम् करोमि। अधुना अपि मह्यम् तत् मन्दिरम् रोचते।
comprehensionPool.cue: As a child I went to the temple every day. Now I work in the city. I still like that temple.

comprehensionPool.display: akasmāt mama śirasi vedanā āsīt. bhavān auṣadham pibatu iti vaidyaḥ uktavān. anantaram vedanā na āsīt.
comprehensionPool.script: अकस्मात् मम शिरसि वेदना आसीत्। भवान् औषधम् पिबतु इति वैद्यः उक्तवान्। अनन्तरम् वेदना न आसीत्।
comprehensionPool.cue: Suddenly I had a headache. 'Drink the medicine,' the doctor said. After that the ache was gone.

comprehensionPool.display: yadā aham grāmam gatavān tadā mama mātā santuṣṭā āsīt. ante mahyam āścaryam āsīt, yataḥ sā miṣṭānnam kṛtavatī.
comprehensionPool.script: यदा अहम् ग्रामम् गतवान् तदा मम माता सन्तुष्टा आसीत्। अन्ते मह्यम् आश्चर्यम् आसीत्, यतः सा मिष्टान्नम् कृतवती।
comprehensionPool.cue: When I went to the village my mother was pleased. In the end I was surprised, because she had made sweets.

comprehensionPool.display: prathamam kāryālayam gacchatu. tataḥ tatra ekam patram paśyatu. anantaram śulkam dadātu. ante pramāṇapatram dīyate.
comprehensionPool.script: प्रथमम् कार्यालयम् गच्छतु। ततः तत्र एकम् पत्रम् पश्यतु। अनन्तरम् शुल्कम् ददातु। अन्ते प्रमाणपत्रम् दीयते।
comprehensionPool.cue: First go to the office. Then look at a form there. After that pay the fee. In the end the certificate is issued.

comprehensionPool.display: pūrvam atra vidyālayaḥ āsīt. adhunā atra kāryālayaḥ asti. akasmāt idam nagaram bhinnam.
comprehensionPool.script: पूर्वम् अत्र विद्यालयः आसीत्। अधुना अत्र कार्यालयः अस्ति। अकस्मात् इदम् नगरम् भिन्नम्।
comprehensionPool.cue: There used to be a school here. Now there is an office here. All at once this city is a different one.

comprehensionPool.display: aham adya gṛham gacchāmi iti mama bhrātā uktavān. akasmāt vṛṣṭiḥ āsīt, ataḥ saḥ na gatavān.
comprehensionPool.script: अहम् अद्य गृहम् गच्छामि इति मम भ्राता उक्तवान्। अकस्मात् वृष्टिः आसीत्, अतः सः न गतवान्।
comprehensionPool.cue: 'I am going home today,' my brother said. Suddenly it was raining, so he did not go.

comprehensionPool.display: bālye mama abhyāsaḥ uttamaḥ āsīt. pūrvam aham pratidinam saṃskṛtam paṭhitavān. adhunā na paṭhāmi, ataḥ mahyam duḥkham asti.
comprehensionPool.script: बाल्ये मम अभ्यासः उत्तमः आसीत्। पूर्वम् अहम् प्रतिदिनम् संस्कृतम् पठितवान्। अधुना न पठामि, अतः मह्यम् दुःखम् अस्ति।
comprehensionPool.cue: In childhood my practice was excellent. I used to study Sanskrit every day. Now I do not study, so I am sorry about it.

comprehensionPool.display: yadi aham adhunā paṭheyam tarhi mama abhyāsaḥ punaḥ uttamaḥ syāt. ataḥ adya aham paṭhāmi.
comprehensionPool.script: यदि अहम् अधुना पठेयम् तर्हि मम अभ्यासः पुनः उत्तमः स्यात्। अतः अद्य अहम् पठामि।
comprehensionPool.cue: If I studied now, my practice would be excellent again. So today I am studying.
